narr: A tropical wave moving over South Florida provided an environment for widespread showers and thunderstorms with high rainfall rates on the afternoon and evening of July 27th. Several of these showers and storms were pinned along the sea breeze and very slow-moving, primarily across Broward County.
ev: Reports from emergency managers, trained spotters, and the public of flash flooding near the US 1/Federal Highway corridor from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport south to Hallandale Beach. Many streets had standing water with vehicles stalled, and water rising into homes in Hollywood along 16th Avenue south of Hollywood Boulevard. The east entrance to Fort Lauderdale - Hollywood International Airport was temporarily closed due to flooding.||Fort Lauderdale - Hollywood International Airport measured 6.17 inches of rain, with measured amounts of up to 7.16 in Hollywood. About 4 inches fell in only 1 hour between 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM EDT.
lsr: Entrance to Ft. Lauderdale Airport from East Perimeter Rd. closed due to flooding. Reopened two hours later.
A trained weather spotter reported vehicles stranded with water covering the entire roadway up to the curbs just south of Ft Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport at Griffin Rd and U.S 1.
